priorInvolvementDisclosure: I returned ACCEPT on v19 and Codex returned REJECT. My ACCEPTs in this lineage are now 0 for 3, at v16, v17 and v19. That is a calibration failure with two nameable components. First, detection followed by self-downgrade. At v9 I flagged the D-032 whole-file pin and filed advisory; Codex made it a finding and it was repaired. At v14 I flagged the register omitting advisory ids and filed advisory; Codex made it HAE14-CX-02 and it was repaired. At v19 I wrote up the undefined disposition vocabulary and the absent state for a partial repair in full, then filed advisory; v20 now folds it with a closed registerDispositionVocabulary and an explicit successor refusal for an incomplete blocking repair. Four times I found the right defect and argued myself out of it, and my downgrade reasoning has a constant shape: no live instance is wrong, the convention is followed in practice, the merits are unchanged. Each of those argues that a defect has not yet caused harm, not that it is not a defect. For a rule the artifact itself declares GOVERNING and offers as the mechanical check, incompleteness is the defect, because the rule is the deliverable. I adopt that line this round, with the counterweight that a complete rule whose only shortfall is coverage breadth stays advisory; Codex grades the CA-3 fixture items advisory too, so that half of my calibration is sound. Second, incomplete probe axes. At v19 all twelve of my probes used a well-formed id; I enumerated container shapes and never enumerated the fields of the objects the rules extract, which is exactly where Codex found HAE19-CX-01. This round I enumerated every field the governing rules touch, then checked by direct text search rather than by inference which of them any rule actually constrains. The finding below came from that enumeration, and it includes a point I raised at v17 and dismissed on precisely the reasoning I am retiring.

shouldFix.title: registerCoverageRule validates a round entry's findings but leaves its provenance fields unconstrained: no rule requires the pinned verdict digest to reproduce, and none ties the recorded verdict to the frozen file or to the entry's own severities
evidence: The rule now has six named checks and every one of them is about findings: laneCheck on the (id, severity) set, pairCheck on (lane, id, severity) triples, dispositionCheck on the closed disposition vocabulary, fromVnCheck on repair-array membership, idCheck on findingIdRule, and the extractor's own type and count checks. None reaches the entry's path, sha256 or verdict.

No rule requires the pinned digest to reproduce before extraction. laneCheck says only 'extract (id, severity) pairs via frozenReviewFindingExtractor', and the extractor's lane clause says 'claude2 extracts only from the pinned Claude verdict'. The word pinned identifies which file to read; nothing requires verifying that the file still hashes to the recorded sha256. I searched every string in the 128141-byte artifact for a clause requiring a recorded sha256 to reproduce or be re-measured before use, and for a clause requiring a recorded verdict to equal or be compared against anything: zero hits for both.

The recorded verdict is unconstrained in both directions. Nothing requires predecessorVerdictFindings[N][lane].verdict to equal the verdict field of the pinned file it cites, so an entry could record ACCEPT for a frozen REJECT while its findings set still matched and every stated check passed. Nothing forbids an entry from recording ACCEPT while its own findings[] carries a BLOCKER or SHOULD-FIX, which is a direct contradiction of the standing gate.

That gate is what makes the verdict word load-bearing rather than decorative. The adopted D-125 record in COORD states its decision type as 'Records independent dual ACCEPT (0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX from both reviewers)', so the verdict word plus the finding severities is the condition a coordinator recording asserts. The register asserts both with no check.

The digest half is load-bearing for the same reason the dispatch makes it a standing condition: 'Predecessor-review replacement is not PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT; pins must reproduce.' The protocol treats pin reproduction as a hard requirement, and the artifact's own mechanical check, which exists to make lineage accounting deterministic, does not enforce it on the very files it reads.

This is the same shape as a defect this lineage has already accepted at SHOULD-FIX. HAE18-CX-02 was sustained because the register could launder a disposition that no check compared against pinned evidence; dispositionCheck closed that. The verdict field is now the remaining register assertion with no comparison to the pinned evidence it summarises.

The live data is clean, which bounds this to SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker. Across every lane for v8 through v19 I verified that all recorded digests reproduce, that every recorded verdict equals the pinned file's verdict field, and that no lane records ACCEPT while carrying a blocking severity or REJECT while carrying none.
shouldFix.impact: registerCoverageRule is offered as the mechanical guarantee that a round entry faithfully represents its two frozen verdicts, and resultIfIncomplete says the successor refuses. As written the guarantee covers only the finding set. A successor can therefore record a lane's provenance and outcome incorrectly, or read a drifted verdict file, and the stated check reports the entry complete. The failure is quiet in exactly the way the rule was built to prevent: an entry that misreports a lane as ACCEPT, or that was extracted from content no longer matching its own recorded digest, is indistinguishable from a correct one under every check the artifact states.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Extend registerCoverageRule with a provenance check covering the fields it already records. Require that predecessorVerdictFindings[N][lane].path exist and that its content hash equal the recorded sha256 before frozenReviewFindingExtractor reads it, with a mismatch refusing the successor rather than extracting. Require that the recorded verdict equal the verdict field of that pinned file. Require internal consistency between verdict and the entry's own severities, so a lane recorded ACCEPT MUST carry no BLOCKER or SHOULD-FIX finding and a lane recorded REJECT MUST carry at least one, matching the standing 0-blocker 0-SHOULD-FIX gate the coordinator recordings assert.

advisories.observation: FC-SUBTYPE-CLASS still exercises no CA-3 row despite CA-3 carrying the largest subtype domain including the deferred KEYCHAIN; destinations.actionSubtype still mixes record and serialized class vocabulary in its requiredness clause before restating it serialized; coveredActs still keys the host classes as CA-1-host-head and CA-4-host against the record vocabulary. Both reviewers have raised all three across nine generations, most recently as HAE19-ADV-01/02/03 and my own CLAUDE-HEA19-A2, all correctly registered ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING and correctly absent from the repair arrays.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: These are the case my corrected calibration deliberately leaves advisory: the governing rule is complete and only its fixture population or phrasing is short. The subtype binding is stated normatively in three places, the mapping sentence is immediately restated unambiguously, and the coveredActs keys are labels rather than discriminator literals. Codex has independently graded the same three advisory in every round they have appeared, which is the check that this half of my calibration is not the same self-downgrade error.

My first pass used word matching and produced false hits for at and verdict, which I discarded after reading the actual clauses rather than reporting them, since misreading my own tooling as artifact evidence is a mistake I made at v14.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. Both claimed repairs land completely and I verified each by execution: every one of Codex's id probe values refuses under findingIdRule, which is applied at all three call sites including the FromVN prefix, and the disposition vocabulary is now closed with an incomplete blocking repair refusing the successor rather than being overclaimed as REPAIRED. Custody is clean on every pin, all 61 recorded inputs reproduce, and the full corpus passes every stated check with 70 triples reconciling in both directions and 32 repair entries matching the 32 REPAIRED ids. The finding comes from the method correction I fixed before reading the subject: enumerate every field the governing rules touch, then determine by direct text search which are actually constrained. Three are not. No clause anywhere in the artifact requires a register entry's recorded sha256 to reproduce before the extractor reads that file, and none compares the recorded verdict to the pinned file or forbids a lane recorded ACCEPT from carrying a blocking finding. Both are load-bearing: the dispatch makes pin reproduction a standing condition, and the adopted D-125 record makes the verdict word together with 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX the adoption gate. The live data is clean on all three, which is why this is SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker. I record plainly that I raised the digest half at v17 and dismissed it as covered by remeasurementClause; that reasoning, which is that a general obligation discharges a specific mechanical rule, is the one that produced four under-calls and I am not repeating it here.
